keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. War of the Austrian Succession page, Treaty of Worms (13 September 1743): 'the Austrians ceded all their territories west of the river Ticino and Lake Maggiore, along with lands south of the Po'. The Aix-la-Chapelle page (18 October 1748) has 'Austria cedes minor territories in Italy to Sardinia, including Vigevano', and the Lomellina page 'The area of Vigevano and Robbio ... was also acquired by Piedmont in 1743'. The region is the one kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/4 uses (confidence 2 for the extent). The 1745 union with the Duchy of Mantua (State of Milan page) adds no land here: Austrian Mantua is drawn in the Habsburg dossier.

region.text: the Duchy of Milan as it stood at its Cliopatria shape of 1535

ledger.note: 1535: Francesco II Sforza dies without heirs and the Habsburgs take Milan. 'Francesco II Sforza died without heirs in 1535, opening a new question for the succession to the throne.' The infobox gives 1450-1796 for the duchy.

11 October 1540: Charles V invests his son Philip II. 'installed his son Philip II there with an imperial diploma signed in Brussels on 11 October 1540'; the page also says it 'was ruled by Habsburg Spain from 1556' and that Henry II of France recognised the possession 'in 1559, with the Treaty of Cateau-Cambresis'.

1707: Spanish Milan becomes Austrian. The duchy 'passed to Habsburg Austria in 1707 during the War of the Spanish Succession'; 'With the Treaty of Baden, which ended the War of the Spanish Succession, the Duchy of Milan was ceded to the Austrian Habsburgs' (1714).

region.text: the Milanese districts (Alessandria, part of Lomellina) ceded in 1713: the 8 cells Cliopatria adds in 1713 beyond Sicily

ledger.note: 11 April 1713: parts of the Duchy of Milan pass to Savoy. Peace of Utrecht page: 'Savoy receiving Sicily and parts of the Duchy of Milan'; 'The main treaties of peace followed on 11 April 1713'; Spain signed its own treaty with Savoy 'at Utrecht on 13 July'. The page names no district; the Alessandria and Lomellina reading is house-of-savoy /ledger/24's (the Lomellina page: 'In 1707 ... a part of Lomellina was conquered by the Piedmontese House of Savoy', so part of the land was held by Savoy earlier). The page says the 'bulk of the Duchy of Milan' went to Charles VI (Austria; Spain until 1706-1707). Mirrors house-of-savoy /ledger/24 and habsburg-monarchy /ledger/56.

region.text: Milanese territory held by Franco-Sardinian troops, 1733-1738 (the cells Cliopatria adds in 1734)

ledger.note: October 1733: French and Savoyard troops enter the duchy. War of the Polish Succession page: 'French and Savoyard troops numbering over 50,000, under the command of Charles Emmanuel, entered Milanese territory as early as 10 October'; 'By 3 November, the city of Milan itself had surrendered'; the Austrians 'recovered most of Milan' in November 1734. The region is the cells Cliopatria adds to the Sardinian shape in 1734, as in kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/1 and habsburg-monarchy /ledger/68; it is the part held until 1738, not the whole duchy the page has overrun in 1733-1734.

ledger.note: November 1738: the occupation ends with the peace. 'A preliminary peace was finally concluded in October 1735 and ratified in the Treaty of Vienna in November 1738.' Mirrors kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/2 and habsburg-monarchy /ledger/73.

'Charles Emmanuel III of Sardinia received territories in the western part of the Duchy of Milan west of the Ticino, including Novara and Tortona.' The page is silent on the Oltrepo Pavese. Mirrors kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/3 and habsburg-monarchy /ledger/74.

ledger.note: 13 September 1743: the Treaty of Worms cedes the Milanese west of the Ticino. War of the Austrian Succession page: 'In return for Sardinian support in Lombardy, the Austrians ceded all their territories west of the river Ticino and Lake Maggiore, along with lands south of the Po.' Confirmed in 1748: Aix-la-Chapelle page, 'Austria cedes minor territories in Italy to Sardinia, including Vigevano' (18 October 1748); Lomellina page: Vigevano and Robbio 'also acquired by Piedmont in 1743'. The extent is kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/4's reading (the pages name only Vigevano). Mirrors that entry.

wars.outcome: Milan passed from Spain to Habsburg Austria in 1707, parts of it went to Savoy on 11 April 1713 (Utrecht), and the Duchy of Milan was ceded to the Austrian Habsburgs by the Treaty of Baden (1714).
wars.note: The page gives no battle or year for the conquest of 1706.

zones.text: Milanese territory held by Franco-Sardinian troops, 1733-1738 (the cells Cliopatria adds in 1734)

wars.outcome: French and Savoyard troops overran the duchy in October-November 1733 and the Austrians recovered most of Milan in November 1734; the preliminary peace of October 1735 was ratified in the Treaty of Vienna in November 1738, which gave Sardinia Novara and Tortona.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession

zones.text: the Milanese territories west of the Ticino and Lake Maggiore, ceded at Worms: the 17 cells Cliopatria adds in 1748 (including Vigevano)

wars.outcome: At Worms (13 September 1743) Austria ceded its territories west of the Ticino and Lake Maggiore to Sardinia, confirmed with Vigevano at Aix-la-Chapelle (18 October 1748). The page has Austrian troops capturing Milan in March 1746, which implies an enemy occupation of 1745-1746 that no page dates.

certainty.note: The Cliopatria shape of 1535 is reused; the page records no frontier change in these 178 years and gives no border.

The cessions of 11 April 1713, November 1738 and 13 September 1743 are dated by treaty, but the districts are the Cliopatria cell sets used by the Savoy and Sardinia dossiers, not boundaries from a page.

notes: A one-page colony-type dossier for the Spanish and Austrian Duchy of Milan, which the eu-13-i report suggested; repaired 2026-10-31 after review (verdict fail) with five more pages (Peace of Utrecht, War of the Polish Succession, War of the Austrian Succession, Aix-la-Chapelle, Lomellina; 6 against a 2-5 budget because the review asked for the 18th-century losses). Added: the loss of 11 April 1713 (Alessandria and part of Lomellina to Savoy), the Franco-Sardinian occupation of October 1733 to November 1738, the loss of Novara and Tortona (November 1738) and the Worms cession (13 September 1743, confirmed at Aix-la-Chapelle 1748), with the keyframe split at 1713, 1738 and 1743; the regions are the ones kingdom-of-sardinia and house-of-savoy already use, so the three ledgers agree. Unsettled: (1) the districts of 1713 (the Utrecht page names none; Valenza and Valsesia, named by the reviewer, are on no page opened; the Lomellina page has a part of Lomellina taken by Savoy already in 1707); (2) the Oltrepo Pavese in 1738 or 1743 (neither page names it); (3) the occupation of Milan by the Franco-Spanish army in 1745-1746 (the Austrian Succession page has the Austrians capturing Milan in March 1746; no page opened dates the start); (4) the capital (no page names one); (5) whether Habsburg Spain held the duchy from 1535, 1540 or 1556; (6) the 1745 union with Mantua (State of Milan page) against 1708 on the Mantua page: Austrian Mantua is the Habsburg dossier's; (7) the cession to the Cisalpine Republic (1797 here, dissolve 1796 as the infobox has it). Orchestrator decision still open (review, /ledger/0): this dossier draws the same land as kingdom-of-spain /ledger/3 (1535 gain of Milan) and habsburg-monarchy /ledger/50 (1707 gain), and neither records a vassal relation with state-of-milan; either those two dossiers add vassal_start/vassal_end naming state-of-milan or this colony layer is dropped. Gazetteer names: none.
